studies.name: Agent Mental Clinic (AMC)
studies.title: Depression Diagnosis Dialogue Simulation: Self-improving Psychiatrist with Tertiary Memory
studies.publication_status: arXiv preprint; no later journal/conference record identified in the current arXiv metadata and exact-title search (checked 2026-10-19)
studies.version: Submission history From: Kunyao Lan [ view email ] [v1] Fri, 20 Sep 2024 14:25:08 UTC (1,994 KB) [v2] Wed, 9 Oct 2024 04:37:29 UTC (1,994 KB)
studies.update_target: Diagnostic skills, encounter/EMR memory, and outcome-dependent memory-importance scores.
studies.fixed_components: Frozen GPT-3.5; constant dialogue, diagnosis and skill-reflection prompts; fixed supervisor stages and relevance/importance sampling formula.
studies.feedback: Professional D4 risk labels, revealed after diagnosis, guide supervisor reflection; diagnostic correctness increments or decrements retrieved-memory importance.
studies.timing: After simulated training consultations (Quiz); accumulated memory is reused on subsequent patients and in the single-attempt Exam setting.
studies.retained_artifact: Conversation records, summarized EMRs, reusable diagnostic skills, and memory-importance scores.
studies.update_generator: LLM supervisor compares predicted and reference depression/suicide risk and produces corrective skills; a fixed rule updates importance.
studies.selection_and_release: Supervisor-generated skills are written to memory; later retrieval samples ten nodes using fixed relevance/importance weighting. The described workflow does not impose an independent clinical release gate.
studies.independent_evaluation: Separate D4 test cases are evaluated in a single-attempt Exam, using professional reference labels; original versus simulated dialogues and memory/supervisor ablations are reported.
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Memory-off, memory-layer and supervisor ablations test component value; they do not compare an evolved skill-generation procedure with its fixed predecessor.
studies.improver_change: not established: skills and retrieval priorities change under constant reflection prompts and fixed importance-update/sampling rules.
studies.clinical_setting: Chinese depression/suicide-risk classification using D4 dialogue-derived patient simulations and original dialogues; 100 selected training cases and 132 original test cases are described.
studies.evidence_boundary: Retrospective dialogue/simulation evidence, with limited four-class accuracy and poorer simulated dialogue performance. The study explicitly lacks real-time expert feedback and prospective patient assessment.

studies.version: arXiv v3 (2024-10-04) read in full; numbers checked against the EMNLP 2024 Anthology PDF
studies.update_target: A long-term memory of past successful question and code solutions, retrieved as the K=4 few-shot demonstrations (§3.2, Eq. 1).
studies.fixed_components: GPT-4 (gpt-4-0613, temperature 0) backbone, tool definitions, EHR metadata, prompts and Levenshtein-similarity retrieval stay fixed (§3.2, §4.1).
studies.feedback: Ground-truth success of each answer decides memory admission; execution error messages drive within-case debugging only (§3.2, App. F.2).
studies.timing: Online across the evaluated question stream; no separate training split for memory is reported (§3.2, App. F.2).
studies.retained_artifact: Successful past cases (question plus code solution) that replace the original hand-written demonstrations (§3.2, App. H.2 Fig. 9).
studies.update_generator: The agent's own successful solving runs; no separate generator component.
studies.selection_and_release: A case enters memory only when it succeeds against the ground-truth answer; a variant admitting all completed cases is also tested (Table 8).
studies.independent_evaluation: Not reported: success rate is measured on the same question stream from which memory accumulates (§4.1, App. F.2).
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Ablation without long-term memory under the same backbone and prompts on MIMIC-III and eICU (Table 2, Table 7); shuffled-order runs reported as almost no influence (App. F.2).
studies.improver_change: None; the storage rule and retrieval procedure are fixed.
studies.clinical_setting: Multi-hop question answering over structured EHR tables of MIMIC-III, eICU and TREQS (§4.1).
studies.evidence_boundary: Offline benchmark with ground-truth labels used at test time for memory admission; no clinician-facing or prospective evaluation (§4.1, Limitations).

studies.publication_status: J/C (IEEE BIBM 2024; added to IEEE Xplore 2025-01-10)

studies.update_target: Experience vector database containing clinician corrections and prompts.
studies.fixed_components: Qwen-7B, five prompted clinical modules, retrieval/tool interfaces and update routine.
studies.feedback: Doctors add prompts or edit LLM inputs/outputs; all edits and prompts are re-encoded into the vector database.
studies.timing: Feedback retained after human interventions for later similar clinical situations.
studies.retained_artifact: Indexed clinician corrections, prompts and case-derived experience.
studies.update_generator: Fixed recording, encoding and retrieval procedure.
studies.selection_and_release: Clinician intervention; no independent update-release threshold reported.
studies.independent_evaluation: 461 retrospectively collected elderly outpatient prescriptions/clinical records from one hospital; two pharmacist raters and a third for disagreement. No separate adaptation/test split reported.
studies.fixed_procedure_control: With/without HITL comparison; no isolated persistent-memory or changing-improver control.
studies.improver_change: Task experience changes; update procedure and model are not shown to change.
studies.clinical_setting: Polypharmacy review, interaction checks, medication schedules and patient education.
studies.evidence_boundary: Abstract calls the mechanism RLHF, but methods document clinician-edit vector-memory reuse rather than parameter RL. HITL also includes current-case corrections, so its comparison does not isolate cross-case learning. Clinical data are retrospective, and deployment effectiveness is unvalidated.

studies.name: EvoPatient
studies.title: LLMs Can Simulate Standardized Patients via Agent Coevolution
studies.publication_status: Peer-reviewed ACL 2025 main-conference long paper
studies.update_target: Patient demonstration/requirement library and doctor questioning-trajectory library.
studies.fixed_components: Model weights, initial standardized-patient requirements, quality criteria and designed recruitment topology.
studies.feedback: Validated question/answer quality and subsequent usefulness of retrieved library entries.
studies.timing: Dialogue-level storage and reuse during simulated encounters; persist across cases.
studies.retained_artifact: Attention library of question-record-answer-requirement tuples and doctor transition trajectories.
studies.update_generator: Evolving doctor questioning generates patient-learning interactions; attention agent extracts requirements.
studies.selection_and_release: Quality validation before insertion; keep stronger duplicates; remove entries after two harmful uses.
studies.independent_evaluation: Separate disease-transfer assessment and human/GPT-4 preferences; no prospective human-trainee clinical-outcome test.
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Tables 4–5 test doctor evolution and recruitment; patient-impact evolved-doctor condition bundles trajectory, question-pool and profile components.
studies.improver_change: Demonstrated at interaction-generator level: evolved doctors alter patient-training experience. Recursive improvement of the whole coevolution procedure is not established.
studies.clinical_setting: Simulated standardized patients grounded in hospital records and public data; medical-education task.
studies.evidence_boundary: Supports co-adaptive training interactions. Bundled ablations and fixed evaluation/coevolution rules preclude an unqualified strict-RSI claim.
studies.addition_relative_to_current: Adds a measured medical counterpart for environment/interaction-generator adaptation, with a clearly bounded evidence claim.

studies.clinical_setting: LLM-generated, expert-filtered Chinese patient-guidance (triage) dialogues across 98 departments.
studies.evidence_boundary: Synthetic-dialogue benchmark; best GPT-4o accuracy is 37.91% and gains plateau after round 5; no deployment study.

studies.version: arXiv v2 (2025-08-15, comment: Accepted at ACM MM 2025); published version not read
studies.update_target: The agent workflow graph (nodes, edges, conditional, loop and parallel structures) and node system and human prompts (§3.1-3.3).
studies.fixed_components: Backbone LLM (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini or Claude 3.5 Sonnet, temperature 1.0), search-space operations, CLIP image-search tool and reference database, evolution prompts (§3.2-3.3, §4.1).
studies.feedback: Diagnostic errors against ground-truth labels, which the LLM classifies as image-understanding or diagnostic errors (§3.3).
studies.timing: Offline batched iterations over the training split, validated after each batch until validation accuracy converges; final workflow frozen for testing (§4.1).
studies.retained_artifact: The final evolved workflow, e.g. 11 nodes and 5 branches at test time (Table 2).
studies.update_generator: The LLM analyses failures and emits structural and prompt suggestions, reformulated into structured modifications via templates (§3.3).
studies.selection_and_release: Infeasible suggestions are filtered, structural edits pass graph-validity checks, and each updated workflow is checked on the 50-image validation set (§3.3, §4.1).
studies.independent_evaluation: Held-out test splits: 224 Skin Concepts images (before excluding 100 images for moderation or broken links) and 120 Skin Conditions images (§4.1).
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Ablations disabling individual operations (Table 3) and operation levels (Table 4); static IO, CoT and Round Table baselines (Table 1); single seed 42.
studies.improver_change: None; the analysis, suggestion and validation procedure is fixed.
studies.clinical_setting: Dermatology image diagnosis on Skin Concepts (Fitzpatrick17k extension) and the synthetically augmented Skin Conditions dataset (§4.1).
studies.evidence_boundary: Small 50/50 training and validation splits, one seed, one synthetic dataset; offline benchmarks only, no clinician or prospective evaluation (§4.1).

studies.name: MACD
studies.title: MACD: Multi-Agent Clinical Diagnosis with Self-Learned Knowledge for LLM
studies.publication_status: P: arXiv preprint (cs.AI), v1 2025-09-24, v5 2026-08-24; no comments or journal_ref; Semantic Scholar lists only arXiv (checked 2026-11-04). v5 declares an npj Digital Medicine editor conflict, suggesting submission there; no acceptance found.
studies.update_target: Disease-specific Self-Learned Knowledge (general and rare diagnostic concepts) injected into the diagnostician prompt.
studies.fixed_components: Base LLMs (Llama-3.1-8B/70B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B), prompt templates, summarizer and refiner procedures (BioBERT MMR de-duplication to top-7, concept ablation), decoding settings, matching rules.
studies.feedback: Ground-truth diagnosis correctness on learning cases; refiner uses change in learning-set diagnostic accuracy when each concept is ablated.
studies.timing: Offline accumulation over the learning set (K_t to K_{t+1} iterations; number of iterations not reported), then frozen knowledge applied to the test set.
studies.retained_artifact: Per-disease, per-model Self-Learned Knowledge text (Supplementary Tables 10-12), also transferred to other LLMs.
studies.update_generator: Diagnostician diagnoses learning cases with current knowledge; Summarizer agent abstracts insights from correct diagnoses; Refiner agent merges, de-duplicates and removes concepts whose ablation does not lower accuracy.
studies.selection_and_release: Learning cases sampled from cases correctly diagnosed by at least one base agent (90 per disease per agent; all 23 for pericarditis); concepts kept by the refiner's redundancy and causal-ablation filters; no clinician release gate.
studies.independent_evaluation: Held-out MIMIC-MACD test cases never used for learning; comparisons with Mayo Clinic and guideline-derived knowledge, CoT, few-shot and LoRA fine-tuning; cross-model transfer; clinician concept-relevance ratings and a 140-case physician reader study.
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Summarizer-only versus summarizer plus refiner ablation and knowledge-composition ablations under the same pipeline; no evolving-versus-fixed improver comparison.
studies.improver_change: Not established: summarizer, refiner and selection rules stay fixed; only the knowledge text changes.
studies.clinical_setting: Primary diagnosis of seven acute abdominal and chest diseases from MIMIC-IV emergency/inpatient text (history, examination, laboratory results, radiology reports).
studies.evidence_boundary: Single-institution retrospective text vignettes; test set is the non-random residue after success-based learning-case selection; physician comparison on text-only vignettes; number of repeated runs not reported.

studies.name: MedAgentSim
studies.title: MedAgentSim: Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Simulations for Realistic Clinical Interactions
studies.publication_status: Peer-reviewed MICCAI 2025 proceedings paper, LNCS 15968, pp. 362–372; publication date 2025-09-21 verified in Crossref.
studies.version: MICCAI 2025 accepted/published version (official OA PDF); latest arXiv counterpart v2, 2025-10-01.
studies.update_target: Medical-record and reflection-experience buffers used for later diagnostic retrieval.
studies.fixed_components: Doctor/patient/measurement roles; KNN retrieval, chain-of-thought prompting, majority-vote ensemble, and correct-diagnosis storage rule; no model-weight update is part of the described method.
studies.feedback: Reference diagnosis determines whether the initial or reflected diagnosis is correct; benchmark outputs are matched to labels by an LLM evaluator with manual review of accuracy logs.
studies.timing: After each simulated consultation; stored records are retrieved during later consultations before ensemble diagnosis.
studies.retained_artifact: CLIP-embedded successful case records and reflection insights from initially incorrect cases corrected on a second attempt.
studies.update_generator: The doctor reflects on an incorrect diagnosis and retries; the record-store module embeds and retains eligible results.
studies.selection_and_release: Correct initial diagnoses enter the medical buffer; only successful corrected diagnoses contribute reflection insights to the experience buffer; unsuccessful retries are discarded.
studies.independent_evaluation: NEJM, MedQA and MIMIC-IV cases are converted to interactive simulations; LLM diagnosis scoring and data conversions are manually reviewed. A separate protected memory-development/test split is not specified in the full published Methods/Experiments.
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Incremental measurement, memory, chain-of-thought and ensembling ablations compare task pipelines, not evolved versus unchanged experience-generation procedures.
studies.improver_change: not established: experience buffers grow under an unchanged retrieval, reflection, voting and admission pipeline.
studies.clinical_setting: Interactive doctor/patient/measurement simulations derived from public clinical cases and exam data; limited human-role identification assesses perceived realism, not clinical efficacy.
studies.evidence_boundary: Benchmark/simulation results support memory-assisted diagnosis. The human-role study is not prospective care, and cumulative additions of memory/reasoning/ensembling cannot isolate recursive improver gains.

studies.fixed_components: Doctor LLM backbone weights, patient, measurement and moderator agents (GPT-4 patient/measurement), prompts, the N = 20 interaction budget and the case set are fixed.
studies.feedback: Per arXiv v5 Appendix M.2, after each case the notebook-update prompt shows the conversation, the correct diagnosis and the agent's own diagnosis; the published Methods describe ground-truth verification of the final answer.
studies.timing: Online and sequential: the notebook is rewritten after every case and used on the following AgentClinic-MedQA cases.
studies.retained_artifact: A single notebook capped at 1000 characters that the agent overwrites each time and must re-integrate prior notes into (v5 Appendix M.2); the published Methods additionally describe a success-only vector store of reflective takeaways.
studies.update_generator: The doctor LLM itself under a fixed notebook-writing meta-prompt, instructed to write general, non-patient-specific tips from successes and failures.
studies.selection_and_release: No acceptance test, validation gate or human review of notes is described; whatever the agent writes is truncated to the character limit and used on the next case.
studies.independent_evaluation: Not reported as a held-out split: the notebook gain is measured as AgentClinic-MedQA diagnostic accuracy over the same sequential stream in which notes are written (each case is seen before its own note update), with no seeds or intervals for the tool table.
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Compared against a no-tool baseline per backbone and against five other tools (zero-shot, one-shot and reflection CoT, adaptive RAG book and web) on AgentClinic-MedQA, for six backbones.
studies.improver_change: Not reported: the notebook-writing prompt and update procedure stay constant; only the notebook contents change.
studies.clinical_setting: Simulated diagnostic dialogues built from USMLE-style MedQA vignettes (tool experiment), with LLM patient, measurement and moderator agents; no real patients or deployment.
studies.evidence_boundary: Benchmark sub-experiment in simulation with an LLM moderator as judge; the notebook effect is backbone dependent (positive for four models, negative for GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o-mini) and is not tested on held-out cases or in clinical use.

studies.update_target: External Experience Memory Bank of actor heuristics and summarizer salience guidelines keyed by EHR embeddings.

studies.timing: Offline before evaluation on 100 MIMIC-IV-Common training examples per task; the same accumulated memory is then reused on all three test subsets.
studies.retained_artifact: Triplets (EHR embedding, actor experience, summarizer experience), one per training instance.
studies.update_generator: Reflection module that shares the agent's frozen LLM, prompted to extract procedural tool-use heuristics and information-salience guidelines.

studies.update_target: Per-agent FAISS memories holding question context, answer, post-hoc notes and, after incorrect predictions, role-specific reflection entries; model weights are not updated (Sec III-C).
studies.fixed_components: GPT-4o for every role, LangGraph routing (Moderator, Recruiter, specialists, Decision Maker, Ethical Overseer), text-embedding-3-large, top-5 retrieval, and a RAG corpus frozen before evaluation (Sec IV-B).
studies.feedback: Ground-truth multiple-choice label; reflection triggers only when the prediction differs from the label (Sec III-C, Alg. 1).
studies.timing: Alg. 1 writes feedback after each labelled question; Sec IV-B says test questions, predictions and reflections were never written back, so test-time memory was static; the phase that filled it is not reported.
studies.retained_artifact: Role-specific memory entries and corrective reflection entries in FAISS, retrieved top-5 per agent (Sec III-C, IV-B).
studies.update_generator: The same GPT-4o agents produce answers and reasoning summaries; a reflection step writes corrective feedback against the label (Sec III-C).
studies.selection_and_release: No filtering, pruning or validation of memory entries; the authors name pruning and confidence-based retention as future work (Sec V).
studies.independent_evaluation: MedQA official test split and a disjoint MedMCQA subset, evaluated in sequential batches of 50; test-set sizes, seeds and intervals are not reported (Sec IV-A, IV-B).
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Ablation against a multi-agent baseline without memory, reflection or RAG, and feedback-only and memory-only variants (Table IV); no comparison of a revised versus a fixed update procedure.
studies.improver_change: None; the reflection rule and memory format stay fixed.
studies.clinical_setting: USMLE-style (MedQA) and AIIMS/NEET (MedMCQA) multiple-choice exam questions; no patient data.
studies.evidence_boundary: Retrospective exam benchmarks only; Ethical Overseer not clinician-validated; source of test-time memory contents unreported; no uncertainty estimates (Sec IV-B, V).

studies.name: Asclepius
studies.title: Asclepius: An Adaptive Harness for Long-Horizon Clinical Agents
studies.publication_status: C: published in Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026, pp. 44611-44629 (ACL Anthology 2026.findings-emnlp.2094, DOI 10.18653/2026.findings-emnlp.2094); arXiv v1 comment also says EMNLP 2026 Findings.
studies.update_target: The natural-language operating manual (main-agent prompt with triage, treatment-completeness and disposition rules and a presentation-to-management table).
studies.fixed_components: Claude Opus 4.6 backbone, MCP clinical tool interface, hand-curated skills library, subagent prompts extracted from the initial manual, proposer prompt, GPT-4.1 judge and CES simulator.
studies.feedback: Trace-level feedback from completed rollouts: aggregate, per-batch and per-patient LLM-judge scores on four dimensions (graded against gold answer keys), per-turn action records and LLM call audit logs.
studies.timing: Offline, between iterations; each of 10 proposer steps is followed by a full rollout over the same six search batches, and the selected manual is frozen at inference.
studies.retained_artifact: The selected evolved manual M* (v7), plus a filesystem of all prior candidate manuals with their scores and traces that the proposer reads.
studies.update_generator: A separate Claude Code proposer (Opus 4.6) with a fixed system prompt requiring edits grounded in failure patterns seen in at least 3 patients across batches, no patient- or batch-specific knowledge, and substantive edits to the current best manual.
studies.selection_and_release: After 10 iterations the manual with the best overall search-batch score (v7) is selected and reused unchanged on held-out batches.
studies.independent_evaluation: Four held-out batches (48 patients) from the same distribution, never shown to the proposer, with one rollout per configuration; baseline and full system re-graded by four further LLM judges.
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Add-one component ablations and an evolved-versus-initial manual contrast holding skills and subagents fixed; no evolving-versus-fixed proposer test.
studies.improver_change: Not reported; the proposer model, prompt and best-score selection rule are fixed across all iterations.
studies.clinical_setting: Simulated six-hour emergency-department shift in CES (12 patients per batch, 4 beds, 6 nurses, one agent physician) with patient cards from de-identified ED records and GPT-4.1-generated physiology.
studies.evidence_boundary: Simulator-only, LLM-graded, single rollout per batch and single backbone, no expert agreement on Asclepius traces; the evolved manual's marginal held-out gain over skills plus subagents is +0.02 (p=0.883).

studies.title: From Given to Gathered Evidence: Agentic Learning for Longitudinal Medical Reasoning
studies.authors: Minye Shao; Chaohui Yu; Yixuan Wu; Fan Wang; Ling Shao; Yang Long; Jing Wang; Hangjie Yuan; Shang Liu
studies.publication_status: P (arXiv preprint; comment lists code and Hugging Face links only; no journal_ref; no Crossref record found 2026-11-04)
studies.update_target: Full weights of one shared Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct policy acting as Radiologist, Anatomist and Consultant, including the visual pathway (Sec 5).
studies.fixed_components: Tool harness and replayed evidence (Vista3D masks, MedGemma-27B reports), role prompts and tool budgets, Kimi K2.6 rubric judge, a frozen Consultant skill store built from teacher trajectories (Sec 5.1, 5.3, App B).
studies.feedback: Exact-match answer reward, format reward, Kimi K2.6 rubric score with top-2 linkage, and a Causal-KL penalty from an answer-privileged view of the same policy snapshot (Sec 5.4, 5.5, Eq. 7).
studies.timing: Offline: RSFT on screened teacher trajectories, then one epoch of on-policy GRPO with G=8 rollouts per prompt; the trained policy is evaluated frozen (Sec 5.2, 5.3, Fig. 3).
studies.retained_artifact: Post-trained CASE-8B policy weights.
studies.update_generator: The learner's own on-policy rollouts; the refreshed policy snapshot also serves as privileged self-teacher for the OPSD penalty (Sec 5.3, 5.4).
studies.selection_and_release: Last checkpoint of the RL run; RSFT data screened by tool use and a rubric score of at least 0.4 (Eq. 3); no checkpoint-gating procedure described.
studies.independent_evaluation: 4,850 questions from 455 held-out participants (14,135 agent-question evaluations), first-pass exact answer-set accuracy, participant-cluster bootstrap for gaps (Sec 4, App C, App F).
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Component ablation from shared RSFT initialization: RSFT only, GRPO, GRPO+RLAIF, GRPO+OPSD, full (Table 2); the evolving self-teacher is not compared with a frozen teacher.
studies.improver_change: The privileged self-teacher is the evolving policy itself and is refreshed after updates (Sec 5.4); rubric and reward weights stay fixed.
studies.clinical_setting: Longitudinal multi-sequence MRI from UK Biobank baseline and follow-up visits with ICD-10-derived multiple-choice diagnostic questions.
studies.evidence_boundary: Single cohort; labels may be unobservable from images; generated evidence and LLM judges are fallible; utility beyond this cohort untested (Sec 7).

studies.authors: Xiwei Dai; Zijie Meng; Zhiting Fan; Yixuan Tang; Guanyu Jiang; Ziru Niu; Zuozhu Liu
studies.publication_status: P (arXiv preprint; comment '17 pages, 5 figures'; no journal_ref; no Crossref record found 2026-11-04)
studies.update_target: A Counterfactual Diagnostic Evidence Graph of diagnosis, evidence and acquisition-action nodes plus diagnosis-revision edges (Graph Consolidation).
studies.fixed_components: Doctor-agent backbones (Gemini-3-Flash-Preview, Gemini-3.1-Pro, GPT-5.6-Luna, Claude-Sonnet-5), patient environment and tools, 30-turn budget, Qwen3-Embedding and SapBERT matching thresholds (Implementation Details).
studies.feedback: Correctness of each trajectory's ICD-aligned final diagnosis against the reference, then verifier preference shifts under counterfactual evidence edits (Candidate Evidence Mining; Counterfactual Validation).
studies.timing: One offline construction pass: K=4 rollouts per construction case from two Gemini agents; the graph is frozen and shared across all evaluated backbones (Implementation Details).
studies.retained_artifact: Frozen graph with 1,156 nodes and 1,426 relations, including 270 diagnosis-revision edges (Table 6).
studies.update_generator: Failed-successful trajectory pairing (cosine > 0.7), UMLS evidence-atom mapping and counterfactual verification by GPT-5.5 (Implementation Details).
studies.selection_and_release: A candidate is kept only if the preference shift holds in both diagnosis orders; 692 of 2,271 candidates (30.47%) retained (Counterfactual Validation; Table 7).
studies.independent_evaluation: 200 patient-disjoint MIMIC-IDx cases (ID) and 107 AgentClinic-MedQA cases (OOD); accuracy judged by GPT-5.6-Sol; repeated runs or intervals not reported (Benchmarks; Metrics; App A).
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Vanilla agent, self-reflection, Trajectory RAG and Flat Experience baselines from the same construction split, plus a graph without counterfactual validation (Tables 2, 3); no revised versus fixed construction procedure over rounds.
studies.improver_change: None; pairing, mapping and verifier stay fixed; online graph evolution is named as future work (Conclusion).
studies.clinical_setting: Long-horizon interactive diagnosis over MIMIC-IV admissions with notes and matched MIMIC-CXR reports, plus AgentClinic MedQA scenarios.
studies.evidence_boundary: Retrospective records in an interactive environment; LLM-judged accuracy; single construction pass; Claude-Sonnet-5 ID accuracy is below Trajectory RAG (Table 2).

studies.name: ClinVerse
studies.title: ClinVerse: A Realistic Multi-Agent Diagnostic Environment for Training and Evaluating Medical Agents
studies.authors: Sirry Chen; Fangke Chen; Xuanwen Ding; Wei Chen; Zhongyu Wei
studies.publication_status: P (arXiv preprint; no comments or journal_ref; no Crossref record found 2026-11-04)
studies.update_target: External doctor-agent artifacts (skills, SkillBank, utility-scored memory, experience bases, cheatsheet, playbook, tool registry) with Qwen3-32B frozen; Appendix C also updates Qwen3-8B weights by SkillRL-GRPO for 30 steps.
studies.fixed_components: Environment roles (dual-layer patient simulator, laboratory physician with ClinLab-2B, environment controller), rule-based judge, ClinPatient cases, and the Qwen3-32B backbone for the nine Table 2 methods (Sec 2.2, App B).
studies.feedback: Deterministic trajectory-level scores against EHR ground truth: weighted information collection rate, test and abnormal-test coverage, ICD-10 block and three-character accuracy (Sec 2.4).
studies.timing: L1 offline adaptation from 5,000 trajectories; L2 online and L3 methods over 1,000 optimization trajectories (Sec 4.3); whether online updates ran on the 100 test cases is not reported.
studies.retained_artifact: Method-specific persistent stores: Trace2Skill skill directory, SkillRL SkillBank, MemRL intent-experience-utility bank, MedAgent-Zero record libraries, Dynamic Cheatsheet, ACE playbook, STOP improved improver, MCE skill-context pairs, MedRSI tool registry (App B).
studies.update_generator: Each borrowed method's own LLM distiller, reflector, curator or improver working on doctor-agent trajectories; Table 3 also tests MemRL with Qwen3-32B versus GPT-5.6-Luna trajectories.
studies.selection_and_release: Method-specific: MemRL utility re-ranking, ACE curator deduplication, MCE iterative evaluation selection, MedRSI fast-discovery slow-registration over later cohorts; ClinVerse adds no separate release gate (App B).
studies.independent_evaluation: 100 cases randomly sampled from a held-out test set, 5 independent runs, mean and SD (Sec 4.1); ClinVerse-adapted agents tested on AIHospital without further adaptation (Table 4).
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Unadapted Qwen3-32B (L0) under the same environment and metrics, plus fixed-procedure L1/L2 methods beside procedure-revising L3 methods (Table 2); no seed-improver versus improved-improver comparison.
studies.improver_change: STOP applies its improver to its own code and MCE evolves its context-engineering skill (App B), but their effect on later learning is reported only as end performance, not isolated (Table 2).
studies.clinical_setting: Simulated diagnostic consultation built from de-identified hospital and ICU EHRs (MIMIC-IV v3.1, MIMIC-IV-Note, SICdb), 150k cases, ICD-10 primary diagnosis as hidden label (Sec 3.1).
studies.evidence_boundary: Simulated environment scored by the authors' own rules; methods reimplemented (SkillRL parameter-free); many gains within one SD over 5 runs; no clinician review of trajectories; preprint.

studies.name: CodeClinic (clinical autoformalization)
studies.title: CodeClinic: Evaluating Automation of Coding Skills for Clinical Reasoning Agents
studies.authors: Timothy Ossowski; Xinchi Liu; Danyal Maqbool; Vaibhav Dhanuka; Sheng Zhang; Hoifung Poon; Majid Afshar; Tyler Bradshaw; Junjie Hu
studies.publication_status: P (arXiv preprint; no comments or journal_ref; no Crossref or OpenAlex venue record found 2026-11-04)
studies.update_target: Shared library of verified Python functions, one per MIMIC-IV clinical concept (63 concepts), built offline and then given to inference agents (Sec 4.1-4.3).
studies.fixed_components: Inference LLM weights, MIMIC-IV schema and query_db tool, LLM-generated guidelines from PubMed abstracts, verification agent, threshold 0.90, up to 100 iterations; the library built with Qwen3.5-27B is reused for every backbone (Sec 4, Sec 5, App D, App F).
studies.feedback: Accuracy of each candidate function on the 10% verification split (about 100 labeled rows per variant), with per-question error traces fed back to the builder (Sec 4.2, App A).
studies.timing: Offline construction per concept in topological dependency order (about 20 GPU-hours per concept); library frozen as a static resource at inference (Sec 4.3, App I).
studies.retained_artifact: Library of verified concept functions exposed as signatures; later concept builds can search and load earlier verified functions (Sec 4.1, App G.1).
studies.update_generator: ReAct autoformalization agent (Qwen3.5-27B) that explores the schema, retrieves guidelines and writes code (Sec 4.1).
studies.selection_and_release: Function saved to the shared library when verification accuracy reaches 0.90; otherwise the best candidate across iterations is retained (Sec 4.2, App F Algorithm 1).
studies.independent_evaluation: Held-out 90% of compositional queries (56,700 test vs 6,300 train) and the longitudinal ICU surveillance task (2,000 held-out stays, subject-level split) not used to build the library (Sec 3.1-3.2, Sec 5).
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Zero-shot agent with the same schema and query_db tool; GRPO fine-tuning with 50 examples per concept on the same backbone (Table 3, Fig 6-7).
studies.improver_change: Not reported; the build-and-verify procedure stays fixed.
studies.clinical_setting: Retrospective MIMIC-IV ICU EHR: compositional concept extraction (e.g. SOFA, Sepsis-3) and 4-hourly surveillance over 48 h with 13 checkpoints (Sec 3).
studies.evidence_boundary: Single institution; library built by one model; small verification sets; LLM-written guidelines; frontier models run on a 21% subset; longitudinal gains shown only in Fig 6 without a numeric table; preprint.

studies.name: DxEvolve
studies.title: Emulating Clinician Cognition via Self-Evolving Deep Clinical Research
studies.publication_status: arXiv preprint; no later journal/conference record identified in the current arXiv metadata and exact-title search (checked 2026-10-19)
studies.version: Submission history From: Ruiyang Ren [ view email ] [v1] Wed, 11 Mar 2026 11:41:51 UTC (1,166 KB)
studies.update_target: A growing repository of diagnostic cognition primitives (DCPs) that guides later test ordering and diagnostic decisions.
studies.fixed_components: Frozen base LLM; shared action/prompt contract, DCP-construction template, embedding retriever, evaluator and bounded diagnostic action space.
studies.feedback: Accrual-case reference diagnoses, correctness flags, rule-based process feedback and charted clinician test orders guide DCP construction.
studies.timing: Post-encounter consolidation in a dedicated accrual pool; nested exposure-indexed repositories are tested on fixed, non-overlapping evaluation cohorts.
studies.retained_artifact: DCPs with an experience pattern, test-ordering guidance, diagnostic-decision guidance and provenance including exposure index, pathology and source outcome.
studies.update_generator: The same backbone uses a fixed reflection template to distill completed encounters into reusable DCPs.
studies.selection_and_release: DCPs are stored and retrieved by dense pattern similarity; the agent is instructed to use them only when compatible with acquired evidence. Clinician ratings assess sampled DCPs after construction, rather than serving as per-update release approval.
studies.independent_evaluation: Non-overlapping 400-case MIMIC-CDM evaluation; a separate 80-case reader-study split; a 293-case external hospital cohort excluded from accrual; two blinded physicians rate 40 sampled DCPs.
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Backbone-matched DCP-free and retrieval ablations plus exposure curves isolate experiential reuse; no changed-versus-fixed DCP-construction procedure is evaluated.
studies.improver_change: not established: later DCPs receive stronger clinician ratings and improve reuse, but maturation of stored guidance is not evidence that the fixed consolidation/retrieval procedure modifies itself.
studies.clinical_setting: Retrospective EHR-based interactive workups for acute abdominal conditions, plus cross-institution/cross-language external validation; imaging is represented by narrative reports.
studies.evidence_boundary: Stronger external retrospective evidence than simulation-only studies; no prospective patient-outcome trial. The published clinician reference uses full information, so it is not a matched-information superiority comparison.

studies.update_target: Experience-node quality and inter-experience edge weights in a dual-layer graph; optional insertion of newly extracted experiences.

studies.feedback: Scalar task-outcome feedback in [-1,1] recalibrates activated nodes and edges; held-out reliability trials initialize experience quality.

studies.retained_artifact: Indication/contraindication experiences, entity/experience graph, reliability scores, relation weights and accumulated edge-credit state.
studies.update_generator: LLM extraction of successful strategies and failure divergences; fixed credit-assignment equations update graph weights from feedback.
studies.selection_and_release: Experience reliability validation initializes quality; fixed thresholds construct edges; online feedback reweights activated memories for subsequent traversal. No clinician release gate is part of the reported benchmark pipeline.
studies.independent_evaluation: Held-out MedR-Bench diagnosis/treatment cases and five MedAgentsBench subsets; DeepSeek-V3.2 judges reasoning and is also one generator. The relation of online-evolution samples to snapshot test cases is not fully specified in §5.3/Appendices.
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Static GSEM is compared with evolving-memory snapshots, plus retrieval ablations; this isolates graph-state calibration, not a self-revised calibration procedure.
studies.improver_change: not established: feedback changes retrieval-affecting state under fixed update equations; the extraction, traversal and calibration procedures are not shown to revise themselves.
studies.clinical_setting: Public retrospective clinical-reasoning and medical-QA benchmarks; automatic evaluation rather than live clinical interaction.
studies.evidence_boundary: Supports outcome-informed memory selection and graph calibration. It does not establish prospective benefit, clinician-validated updates, or improvement of the memory-update algorithm itself.

studies.fixed_components: Gym with 10 domains, 3,631 tasks (2,657 train, 307 validation), 135 tools, 828K-passage knowledge base, domain policy prompts, 5D reward weights, AgentRunner; EMA rule alpha = 0.995 every 5 steps with hard copy every 30 steps (Sec 3, Sec 4.2, App A).
studies.feedback: Episode-level 5D reward (accuracy 0.25, process 0.20, safety 0.20, format 0.10, coherence 0.10) plus cosine length reward; outcome-conditioned hints given only to the teacher (Sec 3, Sec 4.2).
studies.timing: Online RL during training (60 steps on 8 A100 80GB); no updates at evaluation (Sec 5.1).
studies.retained_artifact: Trained policy checkpoint, evaluated with the same multi-turn AgentRunner, tools and knowledge base (Sec 5.2).
studies.update_generator: Student on-policy rollouts in the gym; an EMA copy of the student, conditioned on outcome hints, supplies per-turn KL targets (Sec 4.2).
studies.selection_and_release: Not reported; results given for TT-OPD at step 60 and GRPO peak at step 55 on the validation set (Sec 5.3).
studies.independent_evaluation: 307 held-out validation tasks from the training distribution; 18 external benchmarks (MC QA, VQA, EHR, long-form QA) with test-set fingerprinting for contamination (Sec 5.1, Table 1, App G).
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Base+AR (same tools and knowledge base, no RL), vanilla GRPO with identical hyperparameters, four OPD variants adding one component each (Table 1, Sec 6.1, Fig 4).
studies.improver_change: The teacher that shapes each update is itself updated as an EMA of the student; ablations compare teacher rules (periodic reset, EMA, EMA plus hints, full) on validation curves, not the learned teacher's contribution alone (Sec 6.1).
studies.clinical_setting: Simulated tool-based clinical tasks (EHR, triage, drug interaction, visual and clinical diagnosis, psychiatry, obstetrics, pathways) and offline medical QA/VQA/EHR benchmarks; no clinician or patient involvement (Sec 3, App A.2).

studies.name: LearnActCoder
studies.title: LearnActCoder: Role-Aware Error Memory for Adaptive Clinical Coding Agents
studies.authors: Meysam Ghaffari; Bhaskar Sen; Nasim Sabetpour; Nina Fatehi; Animesh Agarwal; Carlos Morato
studies.publication_status: P (arXiv preprint; no comments or journal_ref; no Crossref record found 2026-11-04)
studies.update_target: MistakeKDB, a structured JSON error memory; false-negative lessons go to the Coder prompt, false-positive lessons to the Judge prompt (Sec 3.2).
studies.fixed_components: GPT-5 weights, the Coder-Judge workflow with up to three rounds, and CodeLookupDB (192,214 ICD-10-CM and 26,533 CPT/HCPCS entries) (Sec 3.1, 4).
studies.feedback: Mismatches between predictions and reference administrative codes from MIMIC tables (false positives and false negatives) (Sec 3.2, 4).
studies.timing: Offline LEARN phase on 25 labelled notes per dataset, then memory reused unchanged in the ACT phase (Sec 3.2, 4, 5.3).
studies.retained_artifact: Lessons with error category, implicated codes, explanation and transferable lesson, consolidated from 1,028 MIMIC-III LEARN mismatches (Sec 3.2, 5.4).
studies.update_generator: A post-hoc LLM MistakeAnalyzer that sees note, predictions and reference codes and assigns one of six error categories (Sec 3.2).
studies.selection_and_release: Similar lessons are consolidated and frequent patterns prioritized before prompt injection; no separate validation gate (Sec 3.2).
studies.independent_evaluation: Note-level held-out ACT sets: 150 matched MIMIC-III notes (paired bootstrap, Wilcoxon), 250 matched MIMIC-IV notes, 250 and 1,000 memory-only MIMIC-III notes (Sec 4, 5).
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Same pipeline with and without MistakeKDB on identical notes, plus raw-example and reflection-summary memory formats from the same error pool (Tables 1-3); routing policy not ablated; no revised update-procedure test.
studies.improver_change: None; MistakeAnalyzer and routing rule stay fixed.
studies.clinical_setting: ICD-9/CPT coding of MIMIC-III discharge summaries and ICD-10/HCPCS coding of MIMIC-IV notes.
studies.evidence_boundary: Retrospective single-system study; one model family; administrative labels as proxy; taxonomy not coder-validated; CPT/HCPCS performance remains low (Sec 6).

studies.update_target: Two knowledge bases: CorrectKB for correct consultations and ChainKB for reflective analyses of incorrect ones (§3.3).

studies.update_generator: A Chain-of-Thought Reviewer agent summarizes each finished consultation into the KB format (§3.3).
studies.selection_and_release: Routing by ground-truth correctness only; no further validation, pruning or release gate is reported (§3.3).
studies.independent_evaluation: Official MedQA and PubMedQA test sets, five runs with SD; cross-dataset KB transfer (Table 3); VQA-RAD and SLAKE official test sets (App. C.2).

studies.improver_change: None; the reviewer and routing rule are fixed.
studies.clinical_setting: Simulated multi-disciplinary team consultation on exam and research-abstract QA, radiology VQA and self-collected complex cases (§4.1, App. C).
studies.evidence_boundary: Offline benchmarks with labels used for KB admission; no deployment, authors plan shadow-system validation (§6 Limitations); human evaluation on 20 samples (App. C.8).

studies.name: MedExpMem
studies.title: MedExpMem: Adapting Experience Memory for Differential Diagnosis
studies.publication_status: J/C: MICCAI 2026 book chapter in LNCS, pp. 430-440, Springer, published 2026-09-25 (Crossref confirmed); extraction uses arXiv 2605.22872v1, which its comment labels 'MICCAI 2026 Early Accept. Submission Version'.
studies.version: arXiv 2605.22872v1 (2026-05-20, only version listed by the arXiv API on 2026-11-03); the LNCS chapter text was not examined.
studies.update_target: An external, per-model experience memory of structured pairwise differential-diagnosis notes (differentials, confusions, discriminators, decision_rule, error_analysis), indexed by 11 departments and 118 organ/region paths.
studies.fixed_components: VLM parameters are not updated (Qwen3-VL 2B/8B/30B, InternVL3.5 8B/30B, Lingshu 7B/32B); the S-PubMedBert-MS-MARCO retrieval encoder, threshold tau=0.9, top-K=10 and the prompts are fixed.
studies.feedback: On construction cases the agent's diagnosis is compared with the Eurorad ground-truth diagnosis, and the expert discussion (imaging findings and diagnostic reasoning) is supplied when extracting a note from each error.
studies.timing: Offline construction in two passes over 6,228 pre-2025 Eurorad cases (Phase I zero-shot, Phase II re-diagnosis with memory), then inference on 227 cases from 2025; updating memory during the test set is not reported.
studies.retained_artifact: The pairwise differential notes, merged per differential pair, persist as a separate memory library built independently for each VLM.
studies.update_generator: The same diagnostic agent (VLM) extracts each note from its own misdiagnosis, instructed to identify confusion points, discriminators, bidirectional decision rules and its reasoning failure.
studies.selection_and_release: Notes are written only for errors (d != d*); Phase II adds notes for stochastic errors and note deficiencies, refines notes that caused correct-to-incorrect transitions and merges insights into existing pairs; no separate validation gate or human review of notes is reported, and at test time retrieved notes are filtered by threshold, top-K and an agent relevance score.
studies.independent_evaluation: Accuracy on a temporally held-out set of 227 Eurorad 2025 cases versus zero-shot baseline, with retrieval recall/precision and beneficial/harmful case rates; the answer-matching method, number of runs, confidence intervals and significance tests are not reported.
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Zero-shot baseline for all seven models, a PubMed-RAG (top-3 articles) comparison and construction/retrieval ablations, all on Qwen3-VL-8B only for the comparison and ablations.
studies.improver_change: Not reported: the extraction, Phase II refinement and retrieval procedures are fixed by design; the one-round versus two-round construction ablation compares preset procedure variants rather than a procedure that revises itself.
studies.clinical_setting: Retrospective evaluation on Eurorad radiology teaching-file cases (CT, MRI, X-ray, ultrasound with clinical history); no prospective, reader-study or deployment evaluation is reported.
studies.evidence_boundary: Gains are single-benchmark accuracy changes of +1.7 to +7.0 points without reported variance or tests, with harmful (correct to wrong) rates of 1.3% to 5.8% and ablations on one model.

studies.update_generator: GRPO with group-mean-centred advantages updates the policy; a frozen Gemma 4 12B distiller converts each completed consultation exchange into a lesson or discards it, and near-duplicate same-task lessons are replaced.
studies.selection_and_release: Distilled lessons enter memory without outcome checking; at retrieval an LLM judge selects at most one of ten nearest lessons and verifies applicability in a second call, and the trained policy decides whether to use it; no clinical review or release gate is described.
studies.independent_evaluation: Patient-disjoint held-out MIMIC-IV-ED patients (100 for main results, 200 patients/897 encounters for test-time learning) with an evaluation attacker (GPT-5.6-Luna) different from the training attacker; no seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Ablations (untrained policy, no-probing training, local-only with and without RL, reward-term variants) and a paired memory-on versus memory-off test-time run; no comparison of a revised versus fixed distiller, judge, reward or training procedure.
studies.improver_change: Not established: memory and policy parameters change, but the distiller, judge, retriever, GRPO recipe and reward are fixed throughout; the trained policy only indirectly shapes which exchanges are distilled, and this effect on later learning is not tested.
studies.clinical_setting: Retrospective emergency-department replay of MIMIC-IV-ED encounters (disposition, primary ICD diagnosis by CCS category, coded procedure for admitted patients), with synthetic personal identifiers injected and re-identification measured against the de-identified 205,504-patient MIMIC-IV-ED registry.
studies.evidence_boundary: Retrospective replay on de-identified records with synthetic personal details and a registry-conditional k measure; no clinician-facing, prospective or patient-outcome evaluation, and the test-time memory gain is mainly fewer remote messages at near-equal accuracy.

studies.publication_status: Preprint; no formal publication identified in arXiv record or author repository
studies.update_target: Client memory, therapeutic skill tree and shared counseling-model parameters.
studies.fixed_components: Therapeutic hierarchy, reward-based session selection and rejection-fine-tuning objective.

studies.update_generator: Learned skill extractor/manager appends or merges skills; best-of-eight rollouts supply RFT data.
studies.selection_and_release: Highest-reward session continues the trajectory; selected trajectories train the model. No independent skill-release test described.
studies.independent_evaluation: Separate evaluation profiles plus human ratings of 522 dialogues by two psychology-trained graduate raters; simulated clients.
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Memory/planning, skill-evolution and internalization ablations; no dedicated control isolating shared-model improvements as an updater.
studies.improver_change: Reported shared-model learning can affect skill extraction/management; improved update-generation ability is not independently established.
studies.clinical_setting: PsychEval simulated multi-session counseling; 120 training and 20 evaluation profiles per therapeutic school.
studies.evidence_boundary: Response-quality and memory/skill benefits; not measured therapeutic outcomes. Public release lacks the complete post-session skill-evolution pipeline.
studies.addition_relative_to_current: Adds a healthcare-specific skill-to-parameter internalization example and distinguishes shared-model change from proved improver improvement.

studies.name: ReclAIm
studies.title: ReclAIm: A Multiagent Framework for Monitoring and Correcting Performance Decline in Medical Imaging AI
studies.publication_status: Peer-reviewed Technical Development article, Radiology: Artificial Intelligence 8(4):e250923; online 2026-06-03, issue 2026-07-01.
studies.version: Full methods and supplements read from arXiv:2510.17004v2 (2026-06-05); journal title, publication status, authors, DOI and abstract cross-checked with the publisher and Crossref.
studies.update_target: Downstream medical-image classifier weights, through full/partial/head-only fine-tuning or gradual unfreezing; the language-model agent itself is not the trained target.
studies.fixed_components: GPT-4.1 reasoning engine; permanent system prompts, agent roles and predefined Python tools; fixed global decline threshold and parameter-anchoring objective. User prompts may specify the fine-tuning recipe.
studies.feedback: Ground-truth labels for monitoring images/scans produce accuracy, precision, recall and F1 metrics; relative decline against development-test metrics triggers intervention.
studies.timing: User-prompted monitoring cycles compare a separate inference cohort with development-test performance, then conditionally fine-tune on a distinct cohort and re-evaluate the same inference cohort.
studies.retained_artifact: Trained/fine-tuned classifier checkpoints, configurations, evaluation/comparison JSON/CSV files, execution traces and conversational task context.
studies.update_generator: A master LLM agent routes comparison and fine-tuning tasks to specialist agents, which invoke predefined training tools using user constraints or configured defaults.
studies.selection_and_release: A global 5% relative-decline heuristic flags any deteriorating metric; the fine-tuning tool selects checkpoints using validation performance and the workflow rechecks inference metrics. Clinical approval is recommended in discussion, not evaluated as a release gate.
studies.independent_evaluation: Patient-separated development, monitoring and adaptation cohorts are reported. Monitoring labels select adaptation and the same monitoring cohort measures its outcome, so post-update results are not from an untouched final holdout.
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Before/after classifier performance is compared; the paper explicitly lacks scripted or single-agent baselines and direct catastrophic-forgetting assessment. It does not compare changed versus fixed improver procedures.
studies.improver_change: not established: classifier parameters adapt while the LLM, permanent prompts, comparison rule and fine-tuning toolkit remain fixed; selecting a configured training strategy is not evidence of revising the improver.
studies.clinical_setting: Retrospective public MRI, CT and chest-radiography classification datasets; one MIMIC-CXR temporal experiment, with the remaining datasets randomly partitioned from the same distribution.
studies.evidence_boundary: A labeled monitoring-and-retraining prototype, not label-free shift detection or prospective deployment. Reused monitoring data, a single temporal dataset and inconsistent temporal/general split descriptions limit stronger generalization claims.

studies.original_draft_gap: Adds a peer-reviewed radiology example in which agentic orchestration updates a separate imaging model using labeled performance feedback; clarifies the distinction between automated model maintenance and recursive improvement of the agent/improver.
studies.read_scope: Complete main manuscript; Supplement A agent/prompt design, monitoring formula and fine-tuning-tool specification; Supplement B partition protocol; Supplement C actual prompt examples and reproducibility description. Numerical outcome claims are restricted to explicit reported results.
studies.key_result: Eight of 18 model–dataset combinations triggered fine-tuning. Do not restate the abstract as universal restoration within ±2%: detailed cardiomegaly results include residual differences beyond 2% and partial recovery for VGG16.

dataset_protocol_detail.general_partition: Supplement B reports patient-based development/inference/fine-tuning cohorts of 60%/20%/20%. The development cohort is further split into 70% training, 15% validation and 15% test; development-test metrics supply the comparison baseline.
dataset_protocol_detail.monitoring: The inference cohort has ground-truth labels (CSV for image directories or labels in NPZ for 3D data). Its performance metrics both trigger and evaluate adaptation.
dataset_protocol_detail.adaptation: A distinct fine_tuning_dataset is supplied to the fine-tuning agent. Tool documentation permits training/validation and optional test folders, but an experiment-wide internal fine-tuning split ratio is not specified in the reported cohort protocol.
dataset_protocol_detail.temporal_dataset: For MIMIC-CXR cardiomegaly, Supplement B separately describes earliest 40% for development, next 20% excluded as a gap, latest 40% for inference and fine-tuning, after one earliest image per patient. This is not reconciled with the subsequent all-datasets 60%/20%/20% statement; do not silently normalize the ratios.
dataset_protocol_detail.post_update_test: Experimental step V and the supplied NoduleMNIST3D prompts explicitly rerun the fine-tuned checkpoint on the same inference dataset. It remains separate from optimization data but has already informed the adaptation decision.

objective_reporting_notes: The threshold is relative percentage change: ((inference metric - development-test metric) / development-test metric) * 100, not a 5 percentage-point drop.

The supplied formula uses strictly greater than the threshold, while adjacent prose/table uses greater than or equal; retain the paper’s global 5% heuristic wording rather than asserting exact boundary behavior.
Parameter anchoring is implemented, but the main limitations explicitly state that catastrophic forgetting was not directly evaluated; do not claim demonstrated prevention.

Four datasets primarily assess response to sampling variability; only the cardiomegaly dataset uses temporal partitioning. Do not classify all five as prospective or external distribution-shift validation.

studies.title: ReVision3D: Attribution-Guided Recursive Self-Improvement for 3D Medical Perception
studies.publication_status: P: arXiv preprint (v1 26 Sep 2026, v2 2 Oct 2026; comment '28 pages', no journal_ref or DOI); OpenReview lists it only as an ICLR 2027 Conference Submission and Crossref has no record (checked 2026-11-03).
studies.update_target: Reader perception configuration (vision-encoder LoRA blocks, rank, input scale, epochs), the RL training recipe that produces reader weights, the 3D candidate-scoring inference program, and a view-selection program.
studies.fixed_components: Frozen LLM designer, frozen pretrained Qwen3-VL-4B weights (only adapters train), mask-grounded verifier with 5 mm tolerance, system objective J, acceptance rule and four predefined intervention levels.
studies.feedback: Reference-mask verification of localized findings, a mask-grounded training reward, J over false-positive budgets on development patients, and replay-based loss attribution; the designer sees only aggregate trial statistics, attribution summaries and trial histories.
studies.timing: Offline revision rounds on development patients, each accepted change triggering renewed attribution; held-out test patients are read once after all choices are frozen.
studies.retained_artifact: The accepted incumbent system (adapter weights, recipe, inference program) plus an evidence-backed playbook of successful and failed hypotheses and trial registries.
studies.update_generator: A frozen language-model designer (Claude Opus 5 by default) proposes revisions within the level indicated by attribution, screened by replay where possible; perception changes require actual training.
studies.selection_and_release: Training revisions are accepted only if mean dev gain exceeds the incumbent's seed range and every matched seed improves; inference revisions need P(dJ>0) >= 0.9 under paired bootstrap.
studies.independent_evaluation: One-time held-out test on 31 liver and 70 kidney patients with patient-level bootstrap, though Appendix B reports that the 31 liver test patients were also used in earlier liver-study comparisons and only 40 of 70 kidney test patients were unused.
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Equal-compute longer-training control for recipe revisions, frozen-encoder and hand-chosen perception comparisons, and a four-designer swap at the inference level; no evolving-versus-fixed improver test.
studies.improver_change: The training recipe that generates reader weights is revised (one accepted learnability recipe, later recipe proposals rejected), while the designer, attribution, verifier, objective and acceptance rule stay fixed and the playbook's effect on later rounds is not tested.
studies.clinical_setting: Retrospective lesion localization on public de-identified abdominal CT (LiTS liver, KiTS23 kidney); authors state it is not a clinical device and makes no diagnostic claim.
studies.evidence_boundary: Benchmark-only, mask-verifiable lesion localization; routing rule formulated retrospectively and did not schedule the experiments; acquisition never passed the promotion gate; no clinician or patient-outcome evaluation.

studies.name: SEA
studies.title: Joint Optimization of Reasoning and Dual-Memory for Self-Learning Diagnostic Agent
studies.authors: Bingxuan Li; Simo Du; Yue Guo
studies.publication_status: P (arXiv preprint; no comments or journal_ref; no Crossref or OpenAlex venue record found 2026-11-04)
studies.update_target: Qwen3-4B/8B policy weights trained by round-wise GRPO to diagnose and issue memory operations; at deployment the short-term case memory (capacity K) and long-term rule memory change while weights stay frozen (Sec 3.1-3.3, App F.2.2).
studies.fixed_components: Closed-set candidate pipeline (ground truth plus 199 GPT-5.2-ranked distractors, fixed seeds), memory tool schema (list/append/pop/consolidate), reward weights and schedule, decoding settings; weights frozen in the long-horizon stream (Sec 4.1.1, App D, App E.1-E.2).
studies.feedback: Ground-truth diagnosis returned after each case; training reward of +5/-5 for correctness plus a short-term-memory occupancy penalty (alpha = 3), linearly re-weighted across rounds (Sec 3.2-3.3, Sec 4.2.1).
studies.timing: Offline RL on the MedCaseReasoning training split (about 48 GPU-hours on 8 A100 for Qwen3-8B); online memory updates after every case in the ER-Reason stream (Sec 4.2.1, App E.2).
studies.retained_artifact: Outcome-annotated short-term case records and natural-language diagnostic rules consolidated from evicted cases, carried forward across stream rounds (Sec 3.1).
studies.update_generator: The trained policy itself decides when to append or pop cases and writes the consolidated rules through tool calls (Sec 3.1, App E.1).
studies.selection_and_release: No gate on memory writes beyond the agent's own consolidate actions; training checkpoint chosen by best validation accuracy (Sec 3.1, App E.2).
studies.independent_evaluation: MedCaseReasoning official test split (each case independent, 10 training cases as memory context, App F.2.3); ER-Reason never trained on and streamed once with frozen weights (Sec 4.2.1, Table 4).
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Same dual-memory tool and prompt with untrained or SFT writers (Qwen-8b SFT + Dual Memory, GPT-5.2 + Dual Memory) and memoryless SFT/RL baselines (Table 2); component ablations on MedCaseReasoning (Table 3).
studies.improver_change: RL with a memory reward revises the policy that writes memory, and stream gains are compared with untrained writers using the identical memory tool (Table 2); writer and diagnostician share weights, so the improver effect is not separated from reasoning gains.
studies.clinical_setting: Closed-set diagnosis (1 of 200 candidates) from published case reports (MedCaseReasoning) and emergency-room cases (ER-Reason); no deployment (Sec 4, App B).
studies.evidence_boundary: Closed-set labels with immediate ground-truth feedback; one stream order, no seeds or intervals for stream metrics; Table 1 and Table 3 gains come from a setting without cross-case carryover; rule quality rated by one internal medicine resident; preprint.

studies.publication_status: P: arXiv preprint (q-bio.OT), v1 only, submitted 2026-10-09; no comments or journal_ref on arXiv, and no Crossref, OpenReview or OpenAlex venue record found (OpenAlex lists only the arXiv preprint; checked 2026-11-03).
studies.update_target: A free-text clinical skill document in the system prompt, which starts empty and is edited by add, replace or delete operations.
studies.fixed_components: Frozen DeepSeek-Flash backbone, fixed task description, fixed Self-Harness loop and acceptance rule, fixed LLM judge, deterministic lookup patient simulator and 10-action budget.
studies.feedback: For each failed held-in consultation, per-metric outcomes plus the reference syndrome, treatment principle, error rubric and the monograph's original expert analysis with full prescription; the ablation sees only per-metric right/wrong.
studies.timing: Offline batch rounds (9 rounds, one proposal per round, seed 42) on fixed development sets before sealed test evaluation; no updating during test or deployment.
studies.retained_artifact: The accepted skill-document text; two edits were accepted (rounds 1 and 6), both short pre-submission checklists.
studies.update_generator: The same LLM that consults diagnoses failed held-in cases into signatures, clusters and ranks them into a brief with successful cases as regression checks, and proposes one minimal edit or declines.
studies.selection_and_release: An edit is accepted only if the summed composite score does not drop on either the 80-episode held-in set (drawn from training) or the 153-episode validation (held-out) set and rises on at least one; no clinician review before release is reported.
studies.independent_evaluation: Sealed 141-episode test split from the same three monographs, not used in selection, each final skill document run three times and averaged, scored by a fixed DeepSeek-Flash judge (temperature 0) plus exact-match and set-based metrics.
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Base harness (empty document) and a learning-signal ablation (outcome-only feedback) under the same loop; no comparison of an evolved versus fixed edit-generating or gating procedure.
studies.improver_change: Not established: the diagnose-propose-gate procedure, prompts and acceptance rule stay fixed across rounds, and only the skill document changes.
studies.clinical_setting: TCM consultation after failed treatment (syndrome differentiation, recognition of the prior physician's error, corrective treatment principle), using 820 episodes digitized from three published misdiagnosis monographs with a deterministic simulator rather than live patients.
studies.evidence_boundary: Retrospective, simulated benchmark from published case books with one backbone LLM (also used as judge), a single evolution seed and no reported confidence intervals, significance tests or physician assessment of the learned guidance.

studies.name: TEMPLAR
studies.title: TEMPLAR: Agentic Induction and Evolution of Standardized Radiology Reporting Templates from Large-Scale Clinical Corpora
studies.publication_status: P: arXiv preprint (cs.MA, cs.CL) submitted 2026-10-04, single version v1; no arXiv comments or journal_ref, and Crossref/OpenAlex searches (2026-11-03) returned only the arXiv record.
studies.update_target: A persistent hierarchical reporting template (slot keys, value types, candidate values, slot-level evidence notes, slot-specific extraction patterns) plus anatomical and diagnostic knowledge graphs built from the training corpus.
studies.fixed_components: Backbone LLMs (Qwen3.6-Flash for induction/evolution, Gemini-3.5-Flash for structuring, reconstruction and diagnosis), text-embedding-3-small, prompts, clustering hyperparameters, the deterministic reducer and the evaluation judges are fixed; no parameters are trained.
studies.feedback: Training-corpus statistics, structural/unit consistency checks, retrieved PubMed/Europe PMC/Google evidence, and one audit of the Clinical Agent's structuring of sampled training findings for collapse to generic values.
studies.timing: Offline, before evaluation: a single construction pass per training split (one round of feedback-guided granularity calibration); the frozen template and graphs are then applied to held-out reports.
studies.retained_artifact: Final template T* with reference notes and extraction patterns, the anatomical graph, the frozen diagnostic graph, and an indexed training-sentence corpus, all with source provenance and audit logs of retrieval queries and rationales.
studies.update_generator: LLM Evolution Agent under fixed prompts proposes assignments, merges, fine revisions, evidence notes and slot-specific patterns P_s.
studies.selection_and_release: A deterministic reducer rejects revisions failing structural or unit checks, slots need more than 3 supporting atoms, vocabularies are supplemented only with training-sentence support, and calibration adds guidance without changing allowed values; no human or clinical release gate is described.
studies.independent_evaluation: Held-out test splits of four datasets scored for LLM-matched template coverage, reference-based reconstruction metrics, LLM-judged diagnostic fidelity (PDA, KFP, CA), and expert plus LLM template-quality ratings; no statistical tests or intervals are reported.
studies.fixed_procedure_control: Cumulative component ablation from ASTAR (M1) to full system (M6), LLM-judged pairwise Revision/Note ablation, and cross-dataset transfer without re-induction; the feedback calibration step is not ablated separately and there is no evolving-versus-fixed updater test.
studies.improver_change: not established: the template and graphs change once under constant prompts, thresholds and reducer rules, and the construction procedure itself is not revised.
studies.clinical_setting: Retrospective English radiology report corpora in whole-body 18F-FDG PET/CT (PETWB-REP, ViMed from a Vietnamese tertiary hospital, machine-translated) and abdominal CT (MERLIN, RadGPT-generated BDMAP reports); no prospective or workflow deployment.
studies.evidence_boundary: Offline corpus-to-template construction evaluated with largely LLM-based metrics on small test splits (n=49 to 408); expert raters are not described, and the authors state that metrics and expert assessments do not establish clinical safety or deployment readiness.

studies.timing: After each clinical task, memories are extracted and statistics updated before the next task.

studies.evidence_boundary: Same-stream sequential adaptation, not an independent post-learning holdout. CN-EHR is externally sourced but also evaluated sequentially. No prospective patient outcomes; memory-on/off and component ablations do not isolate an evolving updater.

studies.update_target: Weights of the attribute sub-agent and the main diagnostic agent (Qwen2.5-VL-3B).
studies.fixed_components: Backbone architecture, crop-and-zoom tool, BUS-CoT attribute taxonomy, reward definitions, GRPO and SFT hyperparameters.

studies.timing: Three sequential offline training stages before testing; agents fixed at inference.
studies.retained_artifact: Trained sub-agent weights, distilled main-agent weights, and the refined trajectory set used for SFT.
studies.update_generator: Stage-2 policy rollouts; the Stage-2 model rewrites rationales of misdiagnosed samples conditioned on ground truth; predicted boxes replaced by ground-truth boxes.
studies.selection_and_release: All sampled trajectories are refined and used; no further selection or validation gate is reported.
studies.independent_evaluation: Held-out BUSBRA, BUSI and BUDIAT splits (BUS-CoT protocol) and external BrEaST OOD set; ablations without oracle training and without self-distillation; GT-box and GT-attribute upper bounds.
studies.fixed_procedure_control: No comparison of a changing versus a fixed improvement procedure.
studies.improver_change: The trained Stage-2 policy also rewrites its successor's SFT data; this role is not isolated from box replacement in the ablation.
studies.clinical_setting: Breast ultrasound image diagnosis (malignancy and BI-RADS) on public datasets.
studies.evidence_boundary: Single 3B backbone and single runs without variance; BI-RADS agreement low (overall kappa 0.224, OOD 0.037); no learning after deployment.
